about: The asset table (package A, 26 Nov 2026; replaces catalogue/distances.json): what a kind of development is like, apart from who's asking (the profile). For each asset type: its names as people say them; the screening scale its size picks (local, regional or global: which of each check's reaches in catalogue/checks.json applies); the footprint radius used when the site is only a point; where it extends a check's reach, with the reason and the source; and the effects it sends out. A check owns its default reach; an asset row only extends it, never cuts it; the person's own distances override both. Protection distances (the developable area's buffers) stay in skills/developable-area/SKILL.md until package D's researched rows are reviewed by Rob. Nothing is fetched beyond 50 km. Read by js/reach.js; tested in test/reach.test.mjs.

fields.names: how people say it, lower case; read from the person's words in code (js/assetwords.js, package E). general.planned lists what has no row (housing, a warehouse): read the same way, screened on the general defaults with its label. counts: words after a number that also name it (a 200-home scheme)
fields.scale: the screening scale for this asset in this setting, with why. by_size rules apply in order, each overriding what it names: below_mw, mw (at least), area_km2 (at least), below_km2. A rule's keeps names a scale whose checks the run also keeps, each check taking the further of its two reaches
fields.footprint_km: the radius of the circle used when the site is only a point: the footprint's own width, which belongs to the place, not a search distance
fields.extends: checks (by id) or topics whose reach this asset extends, to to_km, or by_tip_height ([[up_to_m, km], …, [null, km]]) when the tip height is given. Each has why and source. Never shortens a check
fields.effects: how its effects travel (sight, flight, water, ground, road, sound), each with a source; nothing reads it yet (package E)
fields.pair: the row to use instead when the place is in the other setting (wind farm words for a site at sea read as offshore wind)
fields.scale_source: where the scale and footprint come from. Today these are Tobler's first-cut defaults carried over from distances.json (draft-1, 18 Nov), awaiting package D's research and Rob's review

scale_source: Tobler's first-cut defaults (catalogue/distances.json draft-1, 18 Nov 2026, carried over unchanged as scales on 26 Nov); package D researches them for Rob's review

general.about: An asset with no row (housing, a warehouse, offices, or nothing said): the general defaults for the site's size, and the card says so. A site of 100 km² or more is global whatever it is, and keeps the checks of the scale it would otherwise have had (Rob, 27 Nov).

by_size.why: a site under 1 km² (100 ha): most effects stay within a few kilometres

onshore.why: construction and glint near, traffic and views close, protected sites wider

by_size.why: a small array (under 5 MW): construction effects stay local
a large array (100 MW or more): a bigger land take

onshore.why: noise and shadow flicker near, visual and birds close, protected sites wider

by_size.why: a large wind farm (100 MW or more): wider visual and bird context, keeping the regional checks (heritage, homes, roads, water) as well (Rob, 27 Nov)

extends.why: landscape, visual and cumulative effects of wind turbines: the initial study area by tip height, 45 km for turbines over 150 m (and when the height isn't given, as every recent Scottish scoping report for 175–250 m turbines uses 45 km)
extends.source: NatureScot (SNH), Visual Representation of Wind Farms v2.2 (2017), para 48; scoping reports for Whitelee, Grimshader, Hare Hill and Beinn Tharsuinn (claude/research-reach-evidence.md); Rob's EIA review, 26 Nov 2026

extends.why: the settings of designated heritage assets: wind scoping uses a 10 km outer study area
extends.source: scoping reports for Whitelee (pp.93, 95), Grimshader (pp.42, 44) and Hare Hill (p.82) (claude/research-reach-evidence.md)
extends.not_extended: Listed buildings stay at the check's own reach: towns have hundreds, and the layer's fetch limit would undercount them.

extends.why: Special Protection Areas for wintering geese and other wide-ranging birds: functional linkage to wind farms
extends.source: scoping reports for Whitelee (p.69) and Hare Hill (pp.60–63) (claude/research-reach-evidence.md)

effects.source: NatureScot (SNH), Visual Representation of Wind Farms v2.2 (2017)
NatureScot, Recommended bird survey methods for onshore windfarms (2025)
